chunks: And Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' narrated to me that he was present with Ibn Abi Ya'fur in this gathering.
He said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the discrepancy in hadiths — some narrated by those we trust and some by those we do not trust.

He said: 'Whenever a hadith comes to you and you find a witness for it from the Book of God or from the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), [accept it]. Otherwise, the one who brought it to you is the closest to it [and bears its responsibility].'

key_terms.أَوْلَى بِهِ: most worthy/closest to it — the transmitter is responsible for an uncorroborated hadith
key_terms.اخْتِلَافِ الْحَدِيثِ: discrepancy/divergence in hadiths — the problem of conflicting narrations
key_terms.شَاهِداً: witness/corroboration — a supporting proof from an authoritative source
key_terms.قَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the words of the Messenger of God — authentic prophetic sunnah
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of God — the Quran as primary criterion

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq teach Muslims to resolve conflicting hadiths?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a key principle of hadith authentication within the Shia tradition: when faced with contradictory reports from both trustworthy and untrustworthy narrators, one should verify the hadith against the Quran or prophetic sunnah. If corroboration is found, the hadith is accepted; otherwise, the transmitter bears responsibility for what he has brought. The historical context is a gathering (majlis) of 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur with Imam al-Sadiq, a setting where disciples would pose scholarly questions to the Imam. This criterion — requiring harmony with the Quran and sunnah — became foundational in hadith criticism and is linked to the famous al-Thaqalayn tradition about the two weighty authorities.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, fro Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘And it was narrated to me by Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala that he was present with Ibn Abu Yafour in this gathering where he said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the differing in the Ahadeeth being reported by the ones we trust with it and the ones we do not trust with it’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever a Hadeeth arrives to you and you find evidence for it from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, or from the words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> (fine), or else, the one which came to you which was the closest with it (the Book)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ’Abdallah ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following. “In a meeting where ibn abi Ya‘fur was also present
I asked Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the differences in Hadith which is narrated from people whom we trust and yet from other people we do not trust.”

The Imam replied, “If you come across a Hadith and you find evidence in the holy Quran to support it or in Hadith of the holy Prophet (you may follow it), otherwise, you follow the one that has come to you through the trustworthy narrator.”
